advances: An actual compatible three-fiber path with fixed planar cap normals and prescribed supporting endpoint traces.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Midpoint compatibility and support equality give $(F_A+F_B)/2\subseteq F_K$. The apex $p$ lies strictly inside every other facet inequality of $A$, so its small outward displacement violates only the $F_A$ plane. An added point lies on a segment from this new seed to $A$ crossing the old plane within $F_A$. This gives exactly the triangle over $F_A$.

Minkowski addition distributes over the convex hull defining $A_\varepsilon$. Thus the only new seed set for the middle hull is $(p+\varepsilon n+B)/2$. For each other $K$ facet normal $u$ we have $u\cdot p<h_A(u)$ and hence $u\cdot(p+x)/2<h_K(u)$ for every $x\in B$. The strict slack persists for small $\varepsilon$. Vertices of $B$ off $F_B$ also have strict slack in the $n$ inequality at $\varepsilon=0$. Only the vertices of $J+\varepsilon n/2$ are new outside $K$. The endpoints of $J$ are strictly inside $(F_A+F_B)/2$, hence inside $F_K$. By the same old-plane crossing argument the added region is exactly the asserted trapezoid, a triangle if $L_B=0$. At either extreme integer base only the corresponding endpoint fiber is available, and at zero an anchored combination of the extremes uses equal weights and lies in their midpoint set already contained in $K_\varepsilon$. There are no other integer bases. The area formulas for the triangle and trapezoid give $D$.

Here is the equal-budget argument, which also applies to signed paths. For a scalar middle level $s$ near $s_i^0=v_i\cdot y_0$, take the row with levels $2s-h_i,s,h_i$ at the three bases. At the old body its budget is $Q-s_i(s-s_i^0)+o(|s-s_i^0|)$ by coarea and continuity of the old proper chords. For a path with symmetric differences of area $O(\varepsilon)$ and both $A_\varepsilon,K_\varepsilon$ Hausdorff convergent to the old bodies, the row functions are uniformly $O(\varepsilon)$-close to the old ones, and are continuous strictly decreasing near $s_i^0$, with decrease per unit threshold bounded above and below by positive constants. The upper bounds follow from a common enclosing disk and the lower bounds from a fixed interior disk around $y_0$ in $K_\varepsilon$. The inverse row levels for a proposed budget near $Q$ are therefore continuous strictly decreasing functions of the budget. Their sum has opposite signs at two fixed nearby budgets bracketing $Q$, and is $O(\varepsilon)$ at $Q$. The slope bounds imply its unique zero occurs at $Q+O(\varepsilon)$, with each level $s_i^0+O(\varepsilon)$. The sum-zero levels determine a unique $y_\varepsilon$ near $y_0$ by spanning and $\sum_i v_i=0$. If the fixed-mark increments in the row expansions are $\varepsilon\eta_i+o(\varepsilon)$ uniformly for $s-s_i^0=O(\varepsilon)$, substitution and summation with weights $p_i$ give common budget derivative $\sum_i p_i\eta_i$, since $\sum_i p_i s_i v_i=0$. This argument uses continuity in the row levels for each $\varepsilon$.

For the present additions, vertical slicing of the triangles and trapezoids gives
$\eta_i=\int_{F_A}T_p\mathbf1_{\{v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}}\,ds+\tfrac12\int_{F_K}H_J\mathbf1_{\{v_i\cdot x\ge s_i^0\}}\,ds$.
A proper cut parallel to an added face has a positive gap from its line. A transverse cut crosses the face at most once, and moving the level by $O(\varepsilon)$ affects at most an $O(\varepsilon)$ tangential interval of an $O(\varepsilon)$-high band. This proves the required uniformity and the expression for $q'$. For an exact profile calculation, on $F_K=[a,b]$ and $J=[c,d]$ one has $H_J=[(b-c)T_c+(d-a)T_d]/(b-a)$ by comparison on the three affine pieces.

At the moving mark the middle margins sum to zero, so the caps cover the entire middle plane. Old $A$ traces also cover their plane because $\sum_i b_i=-\sum_i h_i<0$, the strict inequality following from evaluation of the support functions at any interior point of $B$. Consequently both original loads are at least $\min_i p_i>0$ and $q'>0$. The two extreme bases have their ordinary raw depths by 2acc8bc803acf1c0. The maximum on $A_\varepsilon$ is at most the old $A$ maximum plus the added area: for any fixed point all old halfspace masses change by at most that area, and the old depth is zero outside $A$ by separation. The unchanged $B$ maximum is at most $Q$, so both endpoints are below the moving budget for small $\varepsilon$ under the stated $A$ gap. This bounds all candidates. Division by the actual total mass gives the claimed coefficient.
statement:
Let full-dimensional polygons $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ at integer bases $-1,0,1$ satisfy $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Let $v_1,v_2,v_3$ span the plane and sum to zero, and suppose three caps through $(0,y_0)$, $y_0\in\operatorname{int}K$, have thresholds $b_i=2v_i\cdot y_0-h_i$, $v_i\cdot y_0$, and $h_i=h_B(v_i)$ in $A,K,B$, respectively. Assume they have equal raw mass $Q$ and proper cuts in $A,K$. Let $\sigma_{A,i},\sigma_{K,i}$ be the old cutting chord lengths divided by $\|v_i\|$, let $s_i=2\sigma_{A,i}+\sigma_{K,i}$, and let $p_i$ be the normalized weights proportional to $1/s_i$. Define $W_A(x)=\sum_i p_i\mathbf1_{\{v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}}$ and $W_K(x)=\sum_i p_i\mathbf1_{\{v_i\cdot x\ge v_i\cdot y_0\}}$. Write $M=|A|+|K|+|B|$ and $r=Q/M$.

Suppose an outward unit normal $n$ satisfies $h_A(n)+h_B(n)=2h_K(n)$, with exposed faces $F_A,F_K,F_B$ of lengths $L_A>0,L_K,L_B\ge0$, respectively. For $p\in\operatorname{relint}F_A$, put $J=(p+F_B)/2$. For small $\varepsilon>0$ the actual compatible family with $A_\varepsilon=\operatorname{conv}(A\cup\{p+\varepsilon n\})$, $K_\varepsilon=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup(A_\varepsilon+B)/2)$, and $B$ unchanged adds exactly a triangle over $F_A$ and a trapezoid over $F_K$ with top $J+\varepsilon n/2$, up to their bases. Its total mass is $M+\varepsilon D$ with $D=L_A/2+L_K/4+L_B/8$. Write $T_p$ for the unit-height tent on $F_A$ with apex $p$ and $H_J$ for the unit-height trapezoidal profile on $F_K$ which is one on $J$ and decreases linearly to zero at the two endpoints of $F_K$. There is an actual equal-budget middle menu at $y_\varepsilon=y_0+O(\varepsilon)$, with the same continuous normals and $B$ support levels, whose common raw mass is
$$
q_\varepsilon=Q+\varepsilon q'+o(\varepsilon),\qquad
q'=\int_{F_A}T_pW_A\,ds+\tfrac12\int_{F_K}H_JW_K\,ds.
$$
If $Q$ is the old global raw maximum and the ordinary raw maximum on $A$ is strictly below $Q$, then for small $\varepsilon$ this menu bounds the new global raw maximum, even if the unchanged $B$ endpoint ties $Q$. The coefficient of $\varepsilon$ in $q_\varepsilon/(M+\varepsilon D)$ is $C/M$, where $C=\int_{F_A}T_p(W_A-r)\,ds+\tfrac12\int_{F_K}H_J(W_K-r)\,ds$. In particular $C<0$ gives strict normalized descent.
title: Actual enlargement on a shared face of three polygonal fibers
